title: quest init's defaults are wrong for this fleet: interactive never offers Claude Code, and every agent-instructions run writes a per-repo Claude skill regardless of --skill-source
description:
Reported by the user, reproduced by the orchestrator (opum-agent) in a clean temp repo, and independently reproduced and root-caused here in three separate clean temp repos rather than taken on the orchestrator's word. All three are one coherent problem: quest init's defaults describe a world before the marketplace and before Codex was retired as this fleet's runtime, not the fleet actually running it.

1. THE INTERACTIVE WIZARD NEVER OFFERS CLAUDE CODE. runInitWizard (src/cli/main.ts ~599-611) asks exactly three questions -- project name, task ID prefix, and a confirm literally hardcoded as "Write the managed AGENTS.md instructions block?" -- and returns no target field at all. The dispatcher's target variable stays undefined for the entire interactive path, and agentInstructionPathForTarget/updateQuestAgentInstructions/updateQuestSkillFile all default their target parameter to codex (src/application/agents/agent-instructions.ts, five separate = "codex" default parameters, one with the comment "so existing callers are unaffected"). CLAUDE.md is reachable only via the non-interactive --target claude flag, which an interactive user has no way to discover. lore init prompts for this choice; quest init does not, on the same question, in the same fleet. quest init --help / quest manifest --json's own summary text (command-help.ts:34) already states the reasoning precisely: "the default target remains AGENTS.md when --target is omitted, so existing callers are unaffected" -- true and load-bearing for --target flag callers, who have a real back-compat claim; it does not transfer to the interactive prompt, which has no back-compat obligation to anyone, since nobody has scripted against wizard prompt wording. A prompt can ask; only a default has to stay stable.

2. CHOOSING THE CODEX TARGET UNCONDITIONALLY ALSO WRITES A CLAUDE SKILL FILE. Reproduced directly: running quest init --agent-instructions --target codex in a clean repo writes .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md alongside AGENTS.md, every time, with no way to opt out from init itself. Root cause: main.ts's own comment says it outright -- "Explicit beats config: an explicit --agent-instructions request always materializes the skill file, regardless of any persisted agents.skillSource" -- and updateQuestSkillFile() is called unconditionally whenever writeInstructions is true, independent of target or agentSkillSource.

3. --skill-source plugin DOES NOT PREVENT THE SKILL WRITE AT INIT -- confirmed by direct reproduction, sharper than the original report: running quest init --agent-instructions --skill-source plugin in a clean repo STILL writes .claude/skills/quest/SKILL.md. The --skill-source flag's opt-out only governs a later, separate quest agents invocation reading the persisted agents.skillSource config (main.ts ~976-997) -- it has zero effect on init's own write. So even a caller who explicitly asks for plugin-sourced skills at init time gets a per-repo skill file anyway, which the plugin arrangement (opum-quest, federated from release tags, user-scoped) then reports as drift. The default (repo/unset) makes this the out-of-the-box experience for every fresh quest init in this fleet, not just an edge case.

Why these are one problem, not three: every individual default is defensible in isolation as back-compat for scripted --target/--skill-source callers (a real, correctly-identified constraint -- do not remove --target codex, which lore init --codex's public-surface reasoning also protects). Together, on THIS fleet -- Claude Code exclusive, Codex retired as an agent runtime, skills federated from a marketplace -- the out-of-the-box interactive experience writes a retired runtime's instructions file with no offer of the one actually in use, and a decorative-for-this-fleet skill file the plugin arrangement will flag as drift on the very next quest agents --check. quest-cli's own AGENTS.md was deleted under QCLI-230 for exactly this reason (QCLI-227's managed block moved into CLAUDE.md instead) -- this bug is why that cleanup was needed, and every future quest init run in this fleet reproduces the need for it again.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A design decision is recorded first, deserving real thought per the orchestrator: what should the interactive wizard actually ask -- offer a target choice explicitly (claude vs codex, or both), default the confirm text and target to claude for this fleet while keeping --target codex fully available, or something else -- and why

The interactive wizard's prompts (or an added one) let a caller reach CLAUDE.md without needing to already know --target claude exists, while --target's own default and behavior for existing scripted callers (bare --agent-instructions with no --target) stays exactly as stable as it is today

quest init's own skill-file write respects --skill-source at init time (an explicit --skill-source plugin, and per the design decision above, possibly the interactive default too), not only a later quest agents invocation -- explicit beats config is fine as a principle but should not mean an explicit --skill-source plugin is silently ignored by the very command that read it
--target codex and lore init --codex both remain fully available and unchanged as explicit choices -- this is a defaults-and-prompts fix, not a capability removal

Regression tests cover the interactive wizard reaching CLAUDE.md without --target, and --skill-source plugin actually preventing the skill-file write at init, not just changing a later quest agents read

implementationNotes:
DESIGN DECISION (AC1), ruled by the orchestrator (opum-agent) and implemented as ruled:

1. Interactive wizard: must ASK which file (claude or codex), not hardcode AGENTS.md. A bare Enter defaults to claude -- this fleet's runtime, matching what lore init already does on the same question. --target's own unset default for scripted callers (--agent-instructions with no --target) stays codex, unchanged: a prompt can ask, only a default has to stay stable, so no back-compat break for existing scripts.

2. --skill-source plugin given on the SAME command line as --agent-instructions must skip the skill-file write. The prior 'explicit beats config' justification was misapplied: --skill-source given in the same breath is ALSO explicit, not config -- it is explicit versus explicit, and between two explicit instructions the more specific one wins ('do not generate a skill here' is more specific than 'set up agent instructions'). 'Explicit beats config' is kept for its real case: an --agent-instructions request overriding a PERSISTED agents.skillSource from an earlier call.

3. --target codex and lore init --codex both remain fully available, unchanged, as explicit capabilities -- this is a defaults-and-prompts fix, not a removal.
finalSummary:
Fixed, per the orchestrator's ruling (recorded as a note above). All three findings addressed:

1. runInitWizard (src/cli/main.ts) now asks a fourth question -- "Write CLAUDE.md for Claude Code? (no writes AGENTS.md for Codex instead)" -- only when the instructions confirm was yes. Defaults to claude on a bare Enter. Interface change: InitWizardAnswers gained an optional target field, threaded into the init dispatcher (target changed from const to let, set from answers.target only on the interactive path). --target's own unset default for non-interactive callers is untouched -- every default parameter in agent-instructions.ts still defaults to codex, verified live with plain init --agent-instructions still writing AGENTS.md + skill.

2 and 3. The skill-file write (updateQuestSkillFile) is now skipped when agentSkillSource === "plugin" was given on the SAME init call, fixing the explicit-vs-explicit misapplication of "explicit beats config". Verified live across four scenarios: (a) init --agent-instructions --skill-source plugin -- no skill file written, data.skill absent, workspace.toml correctly persists skill_source = "plugin"; (b) bare init --agent-instructions -- unchanged, still writes AGENTS.md + skill; (c) init --agent-instructions --target codex --skill-source repo -- unchanged, writes skill (repo means generate); (d) a PERSISTED plugin config from an earlier call, followed by a later --agent-instructions request that does NOT repeat --skill-source -- still writes the skill once, preserving "explicit beats config" for its real case (overriding persisted config, not an explicit flag given in the same breath).

--target codex and lore init --codex are untouched capabilities -- confirmed unaffected by direct reproduction (scenario c above); lore init --codex lives in a different repository entirely, out of this change's reach.

Regression tests: test/contract/init-wizard.test.ts rewritten for the new four-question flow (5 tests, including the claude-on-bare-Enter default and codex-on-no). test/contract/bootstrap-process.test.ts's QCLI-236 test split into two: one proving the new same-call skip, one proving the persisted-config case still materializes the skill once (the original leftover/drift/force-remove narrative, now correctly triggered by a later call that does not repeat --skill-source rather than by the init call that set it).

CLI help text (command-help.ts's init summary) rewritten to describe the new wizard flow and the explicit-vs-explicit skill-source distinction.

bun run check: typecheck/lint/format/layer:check all pass; 435 tests, 0 fail (was 432; +3 net new tests). 1 pre-existing unrelated lint warning, confirmed present on dev before this branch.
